title: vfps
description: Operational overview of vfps: API traffic and latency, database and connection pool, pseudonym counts, cache, CSV jobs, outbound HTTP and .NET runtime health.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: HTTP and gRPC requests per second across the selected instances. Excludes health probes and the admin UI's SignalR circuit.

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx status. Native gRPC calls always complete with HTTP 200 regardless of their gRPC status, so their failures don't show here - see 'Exceptions thrown by type' below.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route!~"/healthz|/readyz|/livez|/_blazor.*", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route!~"/healthz|/readyz|/livez|/_blazor.*", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration across all selected routes.

panels.title: DB p95
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of database commands issued through Npgsql. A rise here that matches a rise in request latency points at the database rather than the app.

panels.title: DB pool
panels.description: Highest share of the connection pool in use on any instance. A pool near 100% makes requests queue for a connection - see 'Waiting for a connection'.

targets.expr: max(max by (instance, db_client_connection_pool_name) (db_client_connection_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", db_client_connection_state="used"}) / max by (instance, db_client_connection_pool_name) (db_client_connection_max{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Scrape targets currently reachable.

panels.title: Pseudonyms
panels.description: Pseudonyms stored across all namespaces, from the periodically refreshed snapshot.

panels.title: Next token expiry
panels.description: Time until the soonest-expiring unrevoked service-account token expires. Negative means a token has already expired and vfps is rejecting it. Empty if access tokens are disabled.

panels.title: Versions running
panels.description: Instances per running vfps version - more than one series means a rollout is in progress (or stuck).

panels.title: Scrape target up
panels.description: Whether each instance answered its metrics scrape. Gaps or red bands line up with restarts, crashes and OOM kills.

panels.title: Requests by route
panels.description: Request rate per route. gRPC calls are reported as /vfps.api.v1.<Service>/<Method>, REST calls by their transcoded path.

panels.title: Responses by status code
panels.description: Request rate per HTTP status code. 404s are normal for lookups of unknown pseudonyms; a 5xx rise is not.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: Request duration percentiles across all selected routes.

panels.title: p95 latency by route
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration per route - find which endpoint got slow.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route!~"/healthz|/readyz|/livez|/_blazor.*", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval]))), "http_route", "(no route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Latency distribution
panels.description: Request duration histogram over time. Bimodal bands (e.g. a fast cache-hit band and a slow database band) and long tails are easier to see here than in percentiles.

panels.title: In-flight requests & queueing
panels.description: Requests being processed and connections/requests queued by Kestrel. Sustained queueing with low CPU usually means thread-pool starvation (see 'Thread pool') or a saturated database pool.

panels.title: Exceptions thrown by type
panels.description: First-chance exceptions per second by type. RpcException and NamespaceNotFoundException include expected outcomes such as NotFound lookups, so watch for changes rather than absolute values. This is also the only place native gRPC failures show up, since they complete with HTTP 200.

panels.title: Slowest routes (p95 over range)
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration per route over the whole selected time range.

targets.expr: label_replace(sort_desc(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", http_route!~"/healthz|/readyz|/livez|/_blazor.*", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))) > 0), "http_route", "(no route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: Connections per instance by state, with the pool's configured maximum dashed. `used` touching `max` means requests wait for a connection.

panels.title: Pool usage
panels.description: Share of each instance's pool in use.

targets.expr: max by (instance, db_client_connection_pool_name) (db_client_connection_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", db_client_connection_state="used"}) / max by (instance, db_client_connection_pool_name) (db_client_connection_max{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Waiting for a connection
panels.description: Requests queued for a pooled connection and how many gave up after the connection timeout. Npgsql only exports these once requests actually start queueing, so they're empty on a healthy instance. Fix by raising `Maximum Pool Size` (and the database's max_connections) or reducing `CsvProcessing__WorkerCount`.

panels.title: Command latency
panels.description: Duration of database commands issued through Npgsql, across all commands.

panels.title: Commands
panels.description: Database commands per second, and commands executing right now.

panels.title: Pseudonym upsert latency
panels.description: Duration of the batched upsert round trip that every pseudonym write (Create, Append, CSV jobs) goes through. The single-row fallback rate on the right axis counts keys a concurrent writer inserted mid-batch, which are retried one by one - a sustained rate means clients are racing to create the same pseudonyms.

panels.title: New physical connections
panels.description: Physical connections opened per second, and the p95 time to open one. Constant churn means the pool is too small for the load or connections are being dropped. A slow open time points at DNS, TLS or authentication.

panels.title: Database network I/O
panels.description: Bytes sent to and received from the database. Large reads point at queries returning more rows than needed.

panels.title: Prepared statement ratio
panels.description: Percentage of commands that ran as prepared statements. A low ratio under steady load means `Max Auto Prepare` is too small for the number of distinct statements.

panels.title: Pseudonyms per namespace
panels.description: Stored pseudonyms per namespace, refreshed periodically by a background job (so it moves in steps).

panels.title: Pseudonyms added per hour
panels.description: Change in stored pseudonyms per namespace over the previous hour.

panels.title: Largest namespaces
panels.description: The ten namespaces with the most pseudonyms.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of in-memory cache lookups (namespaces and, if enabled, pseudonyms) that were hits. Sampled every 60s, so short ranges look coarse.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(vfps_cache_hits_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) / (sum by (instance) (rate(vfps_cache_hits_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])) + sum by (instance) (rate(vfps_cache_misses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m])))

panels.title: Cache lookups
panels.description: Cache hits and misses per second.

panels.title: Cache entries
panels.description: Entries held in each instance's in-memory cache.

panels.title: Service-account tokens
panels.description: Time left until each unrevoked service-account token expires. Negative means expired. Revoking the old token after a rotation removes its row.

targets.expr: max by (service_account, token_name, token_id) (vfps_service_account_token_expiration_timestamp_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - time()

panels.title: CSV job time by phase
panels.description: Seconds CSV jobs spent per phase, booked when each job finishes. `fetch_input` and `write_output` are object-storage bound (a slow upload shows up as write time), `resolve_database` is database bound, and a growing `report_progress` share points at database round-trip latency.

panels.title: Phase share by direction (over range)
panels.description: Each phase's share of total CSV job time per direction over the selected range.

targets.expr: sum by (direction, phase) (increase(vfps_csv_job_phase_duration_seconds_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / ignoring(phase) group_left sum by (direction) (increase(vfps_csv_job_phase_duration_seconds_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Outbound HTTP latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of outgoing HTTP requests per destination - object storage (CSV jobs), the OIDC provider, a VOPRF key server.

panels.title: Outbound HTTP requests
panels.description: Outgoing HTTP requests per second by destination and outcome. `error_type` is set for connection failures and timeouts that produced no response at all.

panels.title: Outbound connections
panels.description: Open outbound connections, in-flight requests and the p95 time requests waited for a connection.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: CPU cores used per instance, against the number of cores available to it (dashed). Pinned at the limit means CPU-bound or throttled.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Process working set and memory committed by the GC. A working set climbing toward the container limit ends in an OOM kill.

panels.title: GC heap by generation
panels.description: Managed heap size after the last collection, by generation. A gen2 or LOH that only ever grows suggests a leak.

panels.title: GC collections
panels.description: Garbage collections per second by generation. Frequent gen2 collections are expensive and usually follow high allocation rates.

panels.title: Time paused for GC
panels.description: Share of wall-clock time the runtime was paused for garbage collection. Above a few percent, GC pauses show up directly as request latency.

panels.title: Allocation rate
panels.description: Managed memory allocated per second. Drives GC frequency - a jump after a deploy points at a new allocation hot path.

panels.title: Thread pool
panels.description: Thread-pool threads and queued work items. A queue that stays above zero while threads climb slowly is thread-pool starvation, typically from blocking calls on async paths.

panels.title: Thread-pool work items
panels.description: Work items completed by the thread pool per second.

panels.title: Lock contention
panels.description: Times per second a thread had to wait for a contended Monitor lock. Spikes alongside latency point at a hot lock.
